q: Did We not expand your chest
(by increasing your knowledge and granting you the ability to endure the harassment of the Kuffaar)?
v.s: Did We not expand for you, [O Muhammad], your breast?
v.c: Have We not uplifted your heart for you ˹O Prophet˺,

q: And did We not relieve you of your burden...
v.s: And We removed from you your burden

q: (Because of his extraordinary piety, Rasulullaah ﷺ regarded the human mistakes that he sometimes made as serious violations. This was naturally very burdensome for him. By granting him total forgiveness for every single past and future slips, Allaah removed from Rasulullah ﷺ this burden conscience.)
v.s: Which had weighed upon your back
v.c: which weighed so heavily on your back,

q: And We have elevated your mention

(the esteem with which people hold you). (Rasulullaah ﷺ name is mentioned together with Allaah's name in the Kalimah, the Adhaan, the Iqaamah, in sermons and in the introductions of all Islaamic talks and books. When Rasulullaah ﷺ was taken on Mi'raaj, his name was even on the lips of the angels in the heavens. All the previous scriptures contained mention of Rasulullaah ﷺ and all the Ambiyaa ﵊ were commanded to inform their people about the coming of Rasulullaah ﷺ. In the Aakhirah, Rasulullaah ﷺ will enjoy the highest position among Allaah's creation when he attains the status of “Maqaam Mahmood” [see verse 79 of Surah 17]. His fame will then be known to all of Allaah's creation.)
v.s: And raised high for you your repute.
v.c: and elevated your renown for you?

q: (in this world and certainly in the Aakhirah)
v.s: For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease [i.e., relief].
v.c: So, surely with hardship comes ease.

q: Without doubt, there is ease after every difficulty.
(the task of propagating Islaam during the day),
(in other forms of Ibaadah during the night)...
v.s: So when you have finished [your duties], then stand up [for worship].
v.c: So once you have fulfilled ˹your duty˺, strive ˹in devotion˺,

q: (asking for your needs only from Him).
v.s: And to your Lord direct [your] longing.
v.c: turning to your Lord ˹alone˺ with hope.
